title: Composition and flatness for admissible module strict transforms
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open, $f:X\to S$ a morphism, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. (1) For a $U$-admissible blowup $b:S_1\to S$ with centre $Z$ and a $b^{-1}(U)$-admissible blowup $c:S_2\to S_1$ with centre $Z_1$, there is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal on $S$ with zero set $Z\cup b(Z_1)$ whose blowup is isomorphic to $bc$ over $S$. Under this identification the strict transform of $\mathcal F$ along $bc$ is canonically isomorphic to its successive module strict transforms along $b$ and $c$, as modules on $X\times_SS_2$. (2) For any such $b$, if $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$, its strict transform is its ordinary pullback to $X\times_SS_1$ and is flat over $S_1$. In general the strict transform is quasi-coherent, is a quotient of this pullback, and agrees with $\mathcal F$ over $U$; it is of finite type if $\mathcal F$ is. The base $S_1$ is again quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Admissible blowups, centres and module strict transform are as in [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform]; module pullback is as in [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], $b$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Since $S$ is qcqs, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2) makes $S_1$ qcqs. A finite affine cover of $U$, pulled back along the quasi-compact $b$, also shows that $b^{-1}U$ is quasi-compact.

The centre ideals are finite type by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Apply [thm-nagata-composition-of-blowups] (current blueprint_update), with $S$ qcqs and both centre ideals finite type, to obtain $\mathcal K$ with a specified $S$-isomorphism $S_2\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}S$ and $V(\mathcal K)=Z\cup b(Z_1)$. This union misses $U$: a point of $Z_1$ mapping into $U$ would lie in $b^{-1}U$. Thus $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$, since its ideal stalk at every point of $U$ contains a unit. The specified composite is $U$-admissible.

On the associatively identified fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-comparison-epimorphism] to this $\mathcal K$. It gives the epimorphism $\theta:\mathcal F_2\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G$, whose kernel is supported over $V(\mathcal K)$. By [lem-trf-iterated-transform-exceptional-support], that support set equals the inverse image of $Z_1\cup b^{-1}Z$ and $\mathcal F_2$ has no nonzero sections supported there. Every local kernel section is therefore zero; thus $\ker\theta=0$ and the epimorphism $\theta$ is an isomorphism. Its equality after the epimorphism from $(pq)^*\mathcal F$ uniquely determines it, proving the canonical composition assertion.

For a single $b$, [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] gives the quasi-coherent quotient $p^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F^b$ and its isomorphism off $Z$. Since $Z\cap U=\varnothing$, [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] and [def-pc-module-pullback] identify its restriction over $U$ with $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$. If $\mathcal F$ is finite type, so is $p^*\mathcal F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type]; composing its local finite free surjections with this quotient proves finite type of $\mathcal F^b$ [pqf-def-coherent].

If $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$, [lem-pc-relatively-flat-module-pullback] makes $H_1=p^*\mathcal F$ flat over $S_1$, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] makes it quasi-coherent. The exceptional $E=b^{-1}Z$ is Cartier by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]. Apply [lem-trf-relative-flat-cartier-support] to $H_1$ and $E$: it has no supported sections there. Thus the kernel in [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] vanishes. The quotient is an isomorphism, and $\mathcal F^b$ is flat over $S_1$.
